bias.headline: Conditions are clearly bullish (led by Risk Appetite). This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBullish.label: Risk Appetite
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 89th percentile.
topBullish.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are beating safe government bonds by 3.7% — money is willing to take risk to earn more, which usually accompanies a rising stock market.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bullish if it falls out of the top third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than 89% of them

topBullish.label: Volatility
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBullish.explanation: SPY typically moves 0.87% in a day right now — more volatile than 19% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 19% of them

topBullish.label: Market Structure
evidenceFor: Last swing low held; no structural break below 752.18
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 9 swing highs and 10 swing lows over 120 sessions. Confidence scales with how decisively both legs moved relative to the 12% range, and is capped at 75 because a two-pivot sequence is short.
topBullish.explanation: SPY is printing higher highs and higher lows — an intact uptrend. Last swing high 773.50 vs prior 771.25; last swing low 762.63 vs prior 752.18.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
topBullish.nextTrigger: breaks down below the last swing low of 762.63

topBearish.label: Market Breadth
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 82 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
topBearish.explanation: 28% of 82 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually narrow — higher than only 10% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 59%.
topBearish.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 10% of them

watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.13 now
